points: Sisera flees on foot to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber. Jael invites him in, covers him with a mantle, and gives him milk to drink when he asks for water.

He tells her to stand in the door and say no man is there; then Jael takes a nail of the tent and a hammer in her hand, goes softly unto him as he sleeps fast and weary, and smites the nail into his temples and fastens it into the ground, and he dies. The word through Deborah stands: Sisera was sold into the hand of a woman.

Blessed above women in the tent shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be. Sisera asked water and she gave him milk; then she put her hand to the nail and her right hand to the workman's hammer, and where he bowed, there he fell down dead.
